title: Affine pushforward preserves quasi-coherent quotients canonically
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal H$ be a subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with both $\mathcal K$ and $\mathcal H$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and let $q:\mathcal H\to\mathcal Q=\mathcal H/\mathcal K$ be their quotient in the category of module sheaves, i.e. the sheafification of $W\mapsto\mathcal H(W)/\mathcal K(W)$. Then $\mathcal Q$, $f_*\mathcal K$, $f_*\mathcal H$ and $f_*\mathcal Q$ are quasi-coherent and $0\to f_*\mathcal K\to f_*\mathcal H\xrightarrow{f_*q}f_*\mathcal Q\to0$ is exact. Explicitly, on every affine open $U\subseteq Y$, $\mathcal H(f^{-1}U)\to\mathcal Q(f^{-1}U)$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal K(f^{-1}U)$; on every open $U$ the kernel of $(f_*q)_U$ is $(f_*\mathcal K)(U)$. The canonical morphism $\theta:(f_*\mathcal H)/(f_*\mathcal K)\to f_*\mathcal Q$ is the unique isomorphism with $\theta\circ\pi=f_*q$, where $\pi$ is the quotient map. It is natural in morphisms of pairs $(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to i. Its categorical cokernel is quasi-coherent and the cokernel projection is surjective on affine sections. Uniqueness of colimits identifies this cokernel with the specified Q, compatibly with q; hence Q is quasi-coherent and q is surjective on affine sections. The cokernel universal property makes K -> H -> Q exact. Since i is mono, evaluation on any open preserves this exactness by preservation of kernels. Thus ker(q_W) equals range(i_W) on every open W.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] to $\mathcal K,\mathcal H,\mathcal Q$: all three direct images are quasi-coherent. By the definition of direct image, $(f_*\mathcal M)(U)=\mathcal M(f^{-1}U)$, with $\mathcal O_Y(U)$ acting through $f^\sharp_U$. In particular the pushed inclusion is sectionwise injective and the kernel formula of step 1 gives $\ker(f_*q)_U=(f_*\mathcal K)(U)$ on every open $U$. For affine $U$, its inverse image is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; the affine surjectivity in step 1 thus gives exactly the asserted surjectivity on $f^{-1}U$.

proof.text: The categorical cokernel universal property gives t : cokernel(f_*i) -> f_*Q with pi followed by t equal to f_*q. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to f_*i: its cokernel is quasi-coherent and pi is surjective on affine sections with kernel range(f_*i). By left exactness of pushforward and then evaluation, f_*q has this same kernel. For an affine open U, f_*q is surjective by step 2. Consequently t_U is surjective by lifting along f_*q; if t_U(y)=0, lift y along pi_U to x and use the common kernel to conclude pi_U(x)=0. Thus t_U is bijective.

proof.text: The quasi-coherent source and target of $\theta$ satisfy the affine-cover criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-iso-on-affine-cover], so $\theta$ is an isomorphism. Since $\pi$ is an epimorphism, so is $f_*q=\theta\pi$: equality after precomposition by $f_*q$ cancels first the epimorphism $\pi$ and then the isomorphism $\theta$. Together with the sectionwise injectivity and kernel equality from step 2, this proves the stated short exact sequence in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: For a morphism of pairs $a:(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\to(\mathcal H',\mathcal K')$, let $\bar a:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q'$ and $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P'$ be the induced quotient maps. The defining relations give $\theta'b\pi=\theta'\pi'f_*a=f_*q'f_*a=f_*\bar a\,f_*q=f_*\bar a\,\theta\pi$. Cancel the epimorphism $\pi$ to obtain $\theta'b=f_*\bar a\,\theta$, which is naturality. The factorization uniqueness in step 3 also shows that every isomorphism satisfying the required relation is this $\theta$.
